narrative:
Your law school application was denied because the model estimated a 75.8% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, your application was treated as more likely than not to end in bar failure, and that concern outweighed the rest of your file.

The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in decile 2, well below the average of about 5.8 among accepted students. That was the largest influence pushing the prediction toward failure. Your first-year standing was the second-largest factor: decile 3, compared with an accepted-student average near 6.0, also pushed toward failure. Your LSAT score was the third-most influential factor. At 29.30 it was below the accepted average of 37.18, but among these top three factors it was the one that leaned toward passing rather than failing. Your gender and Native American background were not used in the prediction.

To move forward, request an admissions debrief and ask what academic evidence would overcome this bar-readiness concern. Strengthen your record through bar-prep-style study, additional legal writing or analytical coursework, and work with an advisor on a reapplication plan. Consider retaking the LSAT if you can raise it substantially, though your class standing was the larger issue.
